A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HEIST. All 22 pages of v2 and 27 pages of v3, including appendices A–F, support comparison. Text, equations, tables and figures are readable, and retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original HEIST evaluations on imputation, clinical outcomes, cell annotation and clustering, together with component ablations and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds original threshold, loss, initialization and batch-size ablations, attention analyses and ligand–receptor prediction results.

M1.justification: The hierarchical architecture, message passing, decoder and default training objectives remain unchanged. Adaptive threshold selection, spatial batching and feature broadcasting are newly documented details; v2 does not establish contrary implementations. Joint-loss and MLP variants are experimental alternatives, not replacements for the proposed HEIST method.

E1.justification: v3 adds cell-pair ligand–receptor interaction prediction in Appendix E, introducing a biological communication target beyond the original four tasks. The pretraining corpus and existing tissue, organ and technology coverage are retained.

E2.justification: The L4-IT microenvironment comparison expands from scGPT-spatial and CellPLM in v2 Figure A2 to also include STAGATE and GraphST in v3 Figure A3. These methods already appeared in other experiments, but their participation in this specific comparison is new. Main benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include a single-layer ligand–receptor probe on concatenated cell embeddings, evaluation of the top 100 and 1000 attention edges against background/random controls, and 128-versus-256-cell batch experiments. The joint-loss experiment explicitly uses a reduced batch size. Existing benchmark protocols are retained; newly specified pooling and masking details are disclosures rather than established setting changes.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component and positional-encoding ablations, v3 tests adaptive versus constant graph thresholds, individual contrastive terms and a joint objective, MLP-based feature initialization, and batch size. It also adds attention-based biological validation and Braak-stage niche case studies. Tables A6–A11 and Figures A4–A5 substantially broaden the diagnostic and mechanistic evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the five-run mean-and-standard-deviation statement with the same Charville/UPMC exceptions. No new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures are specified. Additional pretraining runs concern new experimental settings rather than an explicitly increased repetition count.

E6.justification: Original scores in Tables 1–4 and A3–A5 are retained, while substantial new results appear in Appendix E. For example, Table A8 reports HEIST's top-1000-edge ligand–receptor rate as 0.279 versus 0.165 background and 0.088 for CellPLM. Table A9 reports prediction AUC-ROC of 0.995±0.002 for HEIST versus 0.984±0.003 for scGPT-spatial. New ablation outcomes and stage-specific qualitative findings further extend the results.

T1.justification: v3 adds asymptotic computational analysis in Appendix C.2 and Table A4, including quadratic attention cost within spatial blocks and dependence on gene edges. v2 reports runtimes without these complexity expressions. No theorem or proof is introduced; most additional preprocessing equations formalize existing descriptions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about hierarchical spatial/molecular modeling, transfer to proteomics, downstream performance, microenvironment discovery and efficiency. The added experiments support these claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v3 extends interpretation from spatial subclusters to ligand–receptor communication and tissue remodeling across Braak stages. It also adds explanations involving threshold-induced graph artifacts, complementary contrastive terms, MLP compression of local signals, and memory-driven batch effects. These substantially expand the biological and mechanism interpretations, although several causal explanations are not isolated experimentally. Appendix F's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices B–D newly specify the cell-type-specific threshold as MI mean plus standard deviation, spatially coherent 256-cell blocks, coordinate/expression broadcasting, and mean pooling for tissue prediction. Imputation masking is quantified as 4 of 30 skin markers and 16 of 200 placenta genes. The layer diagram and discussion of baseline connectivity tuning add further implementation information. These address important ambiguities in v2; code-access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography, Appendix A and novelty positioning relative to hierarchical GNNs and spatial foundation models are unchanged. CellPhoneDB is newly named as an evaluation resource, without a substantive revision of research positioning.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section organization are largely retained. v3 expands the main ablation paragraph, adds explanatory passages in the appendices, corrects cross-references and renames Appendix E from Extra Results to Additional Results. These are localized editorial expansions rather than extensive rewriting or restructuring.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn to clarify projection, masking and decoding, and a detailed HEISTLayer diagram becomes Figure A2. The earlier L4-IT figure is expanded and renumbered A3. New attention and Braak-stage figures and Tables A6–A11 substantially extend the displays; Table A4 gains complexity and interpretation columns. Existing appendix displays are also relocated.

improvement.justification: The threshold, batching and input-shape details reduce implementation ambiguities in v2, while the additional ablations provide useful diagnostic evidence. However, the new ligand–receptor probe lacks clear split and label-construction details, and the joint-loss comparison also changes batch size, limiting stronger biological and mechanistic interpretations. The resulting gain in reproducibility and evidential support is meaningful but qualified.
